result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same clear call on each candidate and give similar, sound reasons. A is tighter and promises a simple in-app toggle; B leaves muting mostly to system settings and adds a toggle only if testing shows demand, and its extra sections make it longer. Neither says that sound and vibration support varies by device and browser, though A at least asks the team to check that the ready chime fires reliably. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make clear per-candidate decisions and save cues for moments when the customer isn't looking. B scores a little higher on the rubric because it commits to an in-app toggle and says to check that the chime fires reliably. Neither answer admits that device and browser support varies or asks for testing on real devices. B also has small flaws: it says sound is 'the only way to reach them' and that a buzz works on silent, which pulls against its own rule about respecting silent mode, and it gets the Android constant name slightly wrong.
